name: Weber anterior colporrhaphy trial
question: Do ultralateral plication or polyglactin 910 mesh augmentation improve anterior colporrhaphy outcomes compared with standard repair?

arms.label: standard anterior colporrhaphy plus polyglactin 910 mesh

design.population: Women undergoing surgery for anterior vaginal prolapse at Cleveland Clinic, including those having concurrent prolapse repairs but excluding planned Burch, sling, or needle suspension procedures.
design.description: Single-center, assessor-blinded, three-arm randomized surgical trial
design.locator: Full text, Methods and Results, pp 1299–1301

verdictNote: Primary anatomic comparison did not meet superiority (log-rank P = .578).
takeaway: In 114 women randomized to standard, polyglactin 910 mesh-augmented, or ultralateral anterior colporrhaphy, the primary anatomic comparison found no significant difference (log-rank P = .578); 83 returned for follow-up at a median 23.3 months.

reports.label: Original randomized report
reports.citation: Weber AM, Walters MD, Piedmonte MR, et al. "Anterior colporrhaphy: a randomized trial of three surgical techniques." *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2001;185(6):1299-1306. doi:10.1067/mob.2001.119081
reports.followUp: Median 23.3 months among women returning for follow-up

results.endpoint: Anatomic cure at points Aa and Ba
results.measure: Optimal stage 0 at both Aa and Ba, or satisfactory stage I at both points with improvement from baseline; 83 follow-up attendees, with the Kaplan–Meier/log-rank primary comparison by randomized assignment
results.note: Primary outcome analyzed by randomized assignment after five exclusions; observed arm proportions are among 83 follow-up attendees. Planned to detect 30-percentage-point differences with 5% type I error. No effect estimate or confidence interval reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods and Results, pp 1300–1302; Fig 2, p 1302

results.measure: Visual analog scale, 1–10, before and after surgery among follow-up attendees
results.note: Within-patient improvement; no arm difference reported and no confidence interval given.
results.locator: Full text, Table II and Results, pp 1302–1303

results.measure: Symptom before and after surgery among follow-up attendees
results.value: 24/82 (29%) preoperatively; 2/82 (2%) postoperatively; resolved in 23/24 (96%) with baseline symptom
results.note: One of 57 women without the baseline symptom reported new onset; no arm comparison reported.

harms.label: Hemorrhage requiring transfusion and pulmonary embolism
harms.value: Hemorrhage requiring transfusion: 1/39 standard repairs; pulmonary embolism: 1/35 ultralateral repairs. No other major postoperative complications were reported.
harms.locator: Full text, Table I, p 1301; Results, p 1302

harms.label: Absorbable mesh exposure
harms.value: One mesh erosion among 35 mesh-group repairs (1/35), treated by office excision of exposed mesh with subsequent vaginal healing.
harms.locator: Full text, Table I, p 1301; Results, p 1302
harms.note: No other mesh-related complications were reported.

delivery.label: Surgery and follow-up
delivery.value: 109/114 underwent an anterior repair; five excluded from all analyses (four did not undergo surgery and one did not have an anterior repair). Five received a different technique from assigned. 83/109 (76%) returned for follow-up; 26 did not (standard 2, mesh 9, ultralateral 15; follow-up imbalance P = .0007).

delivery.label: Technique allocation
delivery.value: All arms received No. 0 polydioxanone suburethral plication and 2-0 polyglactin epithelial closure. Standard repair plicated vaginal muscularis without tension using interrupted No. 0 polydioxanone; ultralateral repair dissected to both pubic rami and plicated paravaginal tissue under tension; the mesh arm fixed a cut-to-fit polyglactin 910 sheet over standard plication with interrupted 2-0 polyglactin.

delivery.label: Concurrent surgery and bladder drainage
delivery.value: Among 109 operated women, the report recorded 57 vaginal hysterectomies, 101 posterior colporrhaphies, 28 enterocele repairs, and 48 vault suspensions. Suprapubic catheters were used in 100 women for a mean 20.4 ± 18.5 days; mean hospital stay was 2.1 ± 0.5 days.

reports.label: Clinical-success reanalysis
reports.citation: Chmielewski L, Walters MD, Weber AM, Barber MD. "Reanalysis of a randomized trial of 3 techniques of anterior colporrhaphy using clinically relevant definitions of success." *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2011;205(1):69.e1-69.e8. doi:10.1016/j.ajog.2011.03.027
reports.followUp: One-year outcomes; retreatment checked through 40 months

results.measure: No prolapse beyond the hymen, no prolapse symptoms, and no retreatment at 1 year
results.note: Overall 66/75 (88%); Table 3 prints 77% beside 20/24 in the ultralateral arm, but 20/24 is 83%. All arm comparisons P > .05; no effect estimate or confidence interval reported.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3 and Results, pp 69.e4–69.e5

results.measure: POP-Q Ba, Bp, and most dependent vaginal point at or proximal to hymen at 1 year; only women with baseline prolapse beyond hymen included, analyzed by assigned arm
results.note: Overall 67/75 (89%); assigned-arm (intention-to-treat) analysis among eligible women with available or backward-imputed follow-up. All arm comparisons P > .05. No prespecified success-rate threshold, effect estimate, or confidence interval reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 69.e2; Table 3, p 69.e5

results.measure: Prolapse visual-analog symptom score at or below 20 mm at 1 year
results.note: Overall 80/84 (95%); all arm comparisons P > .05. No effect estimate or confidence interval reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 69.e2; Table 3, p 69.e5

results.measure: Kaplan–Meier estimate of no prolapse beyond hymen, no prolapse symptoms, and no retreatment with loss to follow-up censored
results.note: Anatomic success 82.3%, symptom success 93.9%, and no retreatment 97.1% at 30 months; no arm difference reported. No confidence intervals given.
results.locator: Full text, Results and Figure 2, p 69.e5

results.measure: Sensitivity analysis counting all participants lost to follow-up as success or failure
results.value: 96/107 (90%) if all lost participants succeeded; 66/107 (62%) if all failed

harms.label: Reoperation for recurrent bulge
harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 69.e4; Table 3, p 69.e5
harms.note: One of 113 women (1%) underwent vaginal vault suspension and enterocele repair at 29 months.

delivery.label: Concurrent prolapse operations
delivery.value: Among 110 with anterior repair, 57/110 (51.8%) had vaginal hysterectomy, 100/110 (90.9%) posterior colporrhaphy, and 50/110 (45.5%) vaginal vault suspension.
delivery.locator: Full text, Results, p 69.e4; Table 2, p 69.e5

delivery.label: Follow-up and allocated treatment
delivery.value: Four of 114 randomized women did not undergo surgery, three received a different assigned repair, and 97 returned for at least one follow-up visit (median 26 months, range 0–172 months). One-year data were imputed by last observation carried backward when later follow-up was available.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 69.e2–69.e3; Results, pp 69.e3–69.e4
